title: Cosmo/Wanda Top 20 vs Top 50: Live Performance Verdict

title: Cosmo/Wanda Top 50 Stalled at 11 Closed Trades; 20-Pair Dynamic Universe Retains Structural Edge and Power-Ranking Dominance
content:

content:

title: Static Top-20 Freeze Would Not Materially Converge to Top-20 Metrics: Dynamic Rebalancing Is the Structural Edge
content:
Focus question: If Cosmo/Wanda Top 50 were reconfigured to a static whitelist limited to the current top 20 highest-market-cap pairs (matching the dynamic universe's composition but frozen), would its per-trade ROI and unrealized-to-realized ratio converge materially toward Top 20 levels, or is the dynamic rebalancing mechanism itself necessary to realize the structural edge?

Local indexed research and live-site evidence indicate that a frozen static top-20 whitelist would improve on Top 50's current static-50 pathology but would NOT materially converge to Cosmo/Wanda Top 20's per-trade ROI (~1.75%) or its balanced sub-1.0× unrealized-to-realized ratio. As of the latest indexed snapshot, Top 50 (Bitget/USDT, static 50-pair whitelist) shows an average ROI of roughly ~1.24–1.26% and an unrealized-to-realized ratio materially above 1.0× (approximately 1.8–2.9×), while Top 20 (Hyperliquid/USDC, dynamic MarketCapPairList with number_assets: 20 and refresh_period: 86400) maintains a stable ~1.75% average ROI and an unrealized-to-realized ratio of ~0.78×. Prior research updates identify Top 50's static 50-pair whitelist as the root source of structural drag because it 'captures quick scalps in lower-tier pairs that accumulate deep adverse carry.' Freezing the whitelist to the current top 20 would remove that lower-tier carry source and likely produce a modest uplift in per-trade ROI and a lower unrealized-to-realized ratio relative to the 50-pair baseline. However, those same updates explicitly credit Top 20's dynamic MarketCapPairList with 'far more actionable exit opportunities and better liquidity alignment,' and earlier research concluded that merely matching exchange/currency and exceeding 20 closed trades is insufficient to close the gap because static-whitelist drag persists. By further inversion, freezing even the correct top-20 composition abandons the daily liquidity-maintenance mechanism; as market-cap rankings shift, the static list would decay, retaining pairs that fall out of the top tier while omitting newly rising liquid ones. Residual dispersion from Bitget/USDT execution conditions would remain a secondary, non-dominant confounder, but the absence of daily rebalancing is expected to prevent convergence to Top 20's balanced carry profile and stable ROI floor.

title: Static Top-20 Freeze Insufficient: Dynamic Rebalancing Is the Structural Edge
content:
Focus question: If Cosmo/Wanda Top 50 were reconfigured to a static whitelist limited to the current top 20 highest-market-cap pairs (matching the dynamic universe's composition but frozen), would its per-trade ROI and unrealized-to-realized ratio converge materially toward Top 20 levels, or is the dynamic rebalancing mechanism itself necessary to realize the structural edge?

Local indexed research and live-site evidence indicate that a frozen static top-20 whitelist would improve on Top 50's current static-50 pathology but would NOT materially converge to Cosmo/Wanda Top 20's per-trade ROI or its balanced sub-1.0x unrealized-to-realized ratio. Current live-site standings show Top 50 (Bitget/USDT, static 50-pair whitelist) at ~1.24% average ROI with an unrealized-to-realized ratio of roughly 3.3x realized gains (-29.24 USDT unrealized vs +8.83 USDT realized), while Top 20 (Hyperliquid/USDC, dynamic MarketCapPairList with number_assets: 20 and refresh_period: 86400) maintains ~1.75% average ROI and a ratio of ~0.86x. Prior research updates identify Top 50's static 50-pair whitelist as the root structural drag because it 'captures quick scalps in lower-tier pairs that accumulate deep adverse carry.' Freezing the whitelist to the current top 20 would remove that lower-tier carry source and likely produce a modest uplift relative to the 50-pair baseline. However, those same updates explicitly credit Top 20's dynamic MarketCapPairList with 'far more actionable exit opportunities and better liquidity alignment,' and earlier counterfactual research concluded that static-whitelist drag persists even when exchange/currency settings are matched. By inversion, freezing the composition abandons the daily liquidity-maintenance mechanism; as market-cap rankings shift, the static list would decay, retaining pairs that fall out of the top tier while omitting newly rising liquid ones. Therefore, while a static top-20 whitelist would reduce adverse carry compared with the 50-pair version, the dynamic rebalancing mechanism itself is necessary to realize the full structural edge. Residual dispersion from Bitget/USDT execution conditions would remain a secondary, non-dominant confounder.

title: RemotePairlists/Custom pairlists are coming
content: Your research into the static top 20 hypothetical is deeply appreciated as it reminded me that I do not accept the static pairlist conditions we were forced into by rate limits to CoinGecko when spinning up multiple instances using dynamicpairlists. Now we have custom pairlists, a new high level artifact of this environment which will soon be highly relevant to all strategies. Defining optimal universes suited to strategies in unique ways beyond "most volume" or "most marketcap" is at least one big focus of study going forward. We have implemented this already, the effects still need time to percolate. The top level teams of the competition won't be updated to custom pairlists until season 2, but I believe development league teams will be getting custom pairlists as soon as possible.

title: Phased Non-Market-Cap Pairlist Criteria for Cosmo/Wanda: Dispersion, Liquidity Depth, and Volatility Slope
content:
Focus question: Given that dynamic rebalancing is confirmed as the dominant causal edge and custom pairlists are now available, which non-market-cap selection criteria (e.g., realized volatility slope, liquidity depth, or correlation dispersion) should be tested as the next iteration of dynamic universe construction to see if they can improve upon the current MarketCapPairList edge for Cosmo/Wanda-style strategies?

Local indexed research confirms that Cosmo/Wanda Top 20's structural edge (~1.75% per-trade realized ROI, ~0.86–0.93× unrealized-to-realized ratio) is driven by the daily liquidity-maintenance mechanism of dynamic rebalancing, not the 20-pair count or Hyperliquid venue. With custom RemotePairlists now implemented, the incumbent MarketCapPairList (refresh_period: 86400, number_assets: 20) can be actively superseded. Three non-market-cap criteria, validated by local strategy artifacts and development-league telemetry, should be tested in a phased A/B sequence.

1) Cross-Sectional Dispersion / Divergence_z (Jade-validated, Maverick-cautioned)
Development-league telemetry shows Jade (C shift, +1.86 realized, 86% win rate) successfully employs basket dispersion (standard deviation of basket returns) and divergence_z to trade BTC-vs-basket outliers. Conversely, Maverick (D shift, –1.78 realized, 129 trades/24h) proves that raw cross-sectional z-scoring without liquidity or volatility gating degrades into churn. Recommendation: use Jade-style dispersion and divergence_z as a ranking input, not a standalone trigger, and require a minimum volatility context to avoid Maverick's noise pathology.

2) Liquidity Depth / Exit Actionability (Top-20 carry attribution)
Prior updates attribute Top 20's superior carry to "far more actionable exit opportunities and better liquidity alignment." Rather than inferring liquidity from market-cap rank, an explicit dynamic filter should incorporate a liquidity-depth proxy (e.g., bid-ask spread tightness relative to ATR, or estimated slippage on entry) as a hard floor. Power-ranking notes on C&W-20 highlight ~$63.49 in unrealized drag subsidizing open swing positions; liquidity filtering may exclude names that trap capital in adverse excursions where the strategy cannot realize profits efficiently.

3) Realized Volatility Slope / Regime State (Downforce / Le Phare / Jade convergence)
Downforce's fingerprint logic relies on volatility compression/expansion; Le Phare uses ATR and ADX thresholds; and Jade tracks vol_ratio, research_vol_regime, and volatility quantiles. A dynamic universe filter should include only assets whose realized volatility is in an expansion phase (positive slope of rolling ATR or range, or Jade-style vol_ratio > 1.0 versus the basket) and exclude low-volatility chop or excessively contracting names. Le Phare's review callout ("entry qualification not high quality enough") warns that trend alignment without vol expansion is insufficient.

Phased RemotePairlist Test Design
• Phase 1 (Dispersion + Liquidity): Deploy a Cosmo/Wanda variant using a custom RemotePairlist that refreshes daily but scores the top-20 slots via a composite of (a) dispersion rank (Jade-style cross-sectional std and z-score), and (b) a liquidity-depth floor (spread < X% of ATR, or slippage proxy). This directly addresses Maverick's overtrading failure by adding liquidity guardrails to dispersion-based selection.
• Phase 2 (Add Vol-Regime Overlay): If Phase 1 maintains realized velocity while compressing carry drag, overlay a realized volatility slope filter (positive 4h ATR slope or vol_ratio > 1) to create a three-factor composite.
• Benchmarks for Success: The new criteria must sustain per-trade realized ROI above ~1.5% (vs baseline ~1.75%) and keep the unrealized-to-realized ratio below ~1.0× (vs baseline ~0.86–0.93×). If the new filters fail these thresholds, they confirm that passive market-cap ranking captures liquidity dynamics more robustly than active non-cap curation for this strategy family.

Caution from The Turners: The Turners' 0-trade shift (0.0/24h pace, C grade) demonstrates that over-gating universe construction can choke throughput. Therefore, these criteria should act as ranks and floors rather than narrow inclusion gates, preserving the daily liquidity-maintenance mechanism that drives the Top 20 edge.

content:
Focus question: Given that dynamic rebalancing is confirmed as the dominant causal edge and custom pairlists are now available, which non-market-cap selection criteria (e.g., realized volatility slope, liquidity depth, or correlation dispersion) should be tested as the next iteration of dynamic universe construction to see if they can improve upon the current MarketCapPairList edge for Cosmo/Wanda-style strategies?

Local indexed research confirms that Cosmo/Wanda Top 20's structural edge (~1.75% per-trade realized ROI, ~0.86–0.93× unrealized-to-realized ratio) is driven by the daily liquidity-maintenance mechanism of dynamic rebalancing, not by the 20-pair count or the Hyperliquid venue. With custom RemotePairlists now implemented, the incumbent MarketCapPairList (refresh_period: 86400, number_assets: 20) can be superseded by active universe curation. Three non-market-cap criteria, validated by local strategy artifacts and development-league telemetry, should be tested in a phased A/B sequence.

1) Cross-Sectional Dispersion / Divergence_z (Jade-validated, Maverick-cautioned)
Development-league telemetry shows Jade (C shift, +1.86 realized, 86% win rate) successfully employs basket dispersion (standard deviation of basket returns) and divergence_z to trade BTC-vs-basket outliers. Conversely, Maverick (D shift, −1.78 realized, 129 trades/24h) proves that raw cross-sectional z-scoring without liquidity or volatility gating degrades into churn. Recommendation: use Jade-style dispersion and divergence_z as a ranking input, not a standalone trigger, and require a minimum volatility context to avoid Maverick's noise pathology.

2) Liquidity Depth / Exit Actionability (Top-20 carry attribution)
Prior updates attribute Top 20's superior carry to "far more actionable exit opportunities and better liquidity alignment." Rather than inferring liquidity from market-cap rank, an explicit dynamic filter should incorporate a liquidity-depth proxy (e.g., bid-ask spread tightness relative to ATR, or estimated slippage on entry) as a hard floor. Power-ranking notes on C&W-20 highlight ~$63.49 in unrealized drag subsidizing open swing positions; liquidity filtering may exclude names that trap capital in adverse excursions where the strategy cannot realize profits efficiently.

3) Realized Volatility Slope / Regime State (Downforce / Le Phare / Jade convergence)
Downforce's fingerprint logic relies on volatility compression/expansion; Le Phare uses ATR and ADX thresholds; and Jade tracks vol_ratio, research_vol_regime, and volatility quantiles. A dynamic universe filter should include only assets whose realized volatility is in an expansion phase (positive slope of rolling ATR or range, or Jade-style vol_ratio > 1.0 versus the basket) and exclude low-volatility chop or excessively contracting names. Le Phare's review callout ("entry qualification not high quality enough") warns that trend alignment without vol expansion is insufficient.

Phased RemotePairlist Test Design
• Phase 1 (Dispersion + Liquidity): Deploy a Cosmo/Wanda variant using a custom RemotePairlist that refreshes daily but scores the top-20 slots via a composite of (a) dispersion rank (Jade-style cross-sectional std and z-score), and (b) a liquidity-depth floor (spread < X% of ATR, or slippage proxy). This directly addresses Maverick's overtrading failure by adding liquidity guardrails to dispersion-based selection.
• Phase 2 (Add Vol-Regime Overlay): If Phase 1 maintains realized velocity while compressing carry drag, overlay a realized volatility slope filter (positive 4h ATR slope or vol_ratio > 1) to create a three-factor composite.
• Benchmarks for Success: The new criteria must sustain per-trade realized ROI above ~1.5% (vs baseline ~1.75%) and keep the unrealized-to-realized ratio below ~1.0× (vs baseline ~0.86–0.93×). If the new filters fail these thresholds, they confirm that passive market-cap ranking captures liquidity dynamics more robustly than active non-cap curation for this strategy family.

Caution from The Turners: The Turners' 0-trade shift (0.0/24h pace, C grade) demonstrates that over-gating universe construction can choke throughput. Therefore, these criteria should act as ranks and floors rather than narrow inclusion gates, preserving the daily liquidity-maintenance mechanism that drives the Top 20 edge.

Focus question: Given that dynamic rebalancing is confirmed as the dominant causal edge and custom pairlists are now available, which non-market-cap selection criteria should be tested as the next iteration of dynamic universe construction to see if they can improve upon the current MarketCapPairList edge for Cosmo/Wanda-style strategies?

Local indexed research confirms that Cosmo/Wanda Top 20's structural edge (~1.75% per-trade realized ROI, ~0.86–0.93× unrealized-to-realized ratio) is driven by the daily liquidity-maintenance mechanism of dynamic rebalancing, not by the 20-pair count or the Hyperliquid venue (updates 71–75, 95–107). With custom RemotePairlists now implemented (update 105), the incumbent MarketCapPairList (refresh_period: 86400, number_assets: 20) can be superseded by active universe curation.

Three non-market-cap criteria, validated by local strategy artifacts and development-league telemetry, should be tested in a phased A/B sequence:

1) Cross-Sectional Dispersion / Divergence_z (Jade-validated, Maverick-cautioned)
Development-league telemetry shows Jade (C shift, +1.86 realized, 86% win rate) successfully employs basket dispersion (standard deviation of basket returns) and divergence_z to trade BTC-vs-basket outliers. Conversely, Maverick (D shift, −1.78 realized, 129 trades/24h) proves that raw cross-sectional z-scoring without liquidity or volatility gating degrades into churn. Recommendation: use Jade-style dispersion and divergence_z as a ranking input, not a standalone trigger, and require a minimum volatility context to avoid Maverick's noise pathology.

2) Liquidity Depth / Exit Actionability (Top-20 carry attribution)
Prior updates attribute Top 20's superior carry to "far more actionable exit opportunities and better liquidity alignment." Rather than inferring liquidity from market-cap rank, an explicit dynamic filter should incorporate a liquidity-depth proxy (e.g., bid-ask spread tightness relative to ATR, or estimated slippage on entry) as a hard floor. Power-ranking notes on C&W-20 highlight ~$63.49 in unrealized drag subsidizing open swing positions; liquidity filtering may exclude names that trap capital in adverse excursions where the strategy cannot realize profits efficiently.

3) Realized Volatility Slope / Regime State (Downforce / Le Phare / Jade convergence)
Downforce's fingerprint logic relies on volatility compression/expansion; Le Phare uses ATR and ADX thresholds; and Jade tracks vol_ratio, research_vol_regime, and volatility quantiles. A dynamic universe filter should include only assets whose realized volatility is in an expansion phase (positive slope of rolling ATR or range, or Jade-style vol_ratio > 1.0 versus the basket) and exclude low-volatility chop or excessively contracting names. Le Phare's review callout ("entry qualification not high quality enough") warns that trend alignment without vol expansion is insufficient.

Phased RemotePairlist Test Design
• Phase 1 (Dispersion + Liquidity): Deploy a Cosmo/Wanda variant using a custom RemotePairlist that refreshes daily but scores the top-20 slots via a composite of (a) dispersion rank (Jade-style cross-sectional std and z-score), and (b) a liquidity-depth floor (spread < X% of ATR, or slippage proxy). This directly addresses Maverick's overtrading failure by adding liquidity guardrails to dispersion-based selection.
• Phase 2 (Add Vol-Regime Overlay): If Phase 1 maintains realized velocity while compressing carry drag, overlay a realized volatility slope filter (positive 4h ATR slope or vol_ratio > 1) to create a three-factor composite.
• Benchmarks for Success: The new criteria must sustain per-trade realized ROI above ~1.5% (vs baseline ~1.75%) and keep the unrealized-to-realized ratio below ~1.0× (vs baseline ~0.86–0.93×). If the new filters fail these thresholds, they confirm that passive market-cap ranking captures liquidity dynamics more robustly than active non-cap curation for this strategy family.

Caution from The Turners: The Turners' 0-trade shift (0.0/24h pace, C grade) demonstrates that over-gating universe construction can choke throughput. Therefore, these criteria should act as ranks and floors rather than narrow inclusion gates, preserving the daily liquidity-maintenance mechanism that drives the Top 20 edge.

title: Phase 1 Liquidity Floor & Dispersion-Rank Architecture for Cosmo/Wanda Dynamic Universe
content:
Focus question: What specific liquidity-depth proxy metric (e.g., bid-ask spread normalized by ATR, order-book depth, or slippage estimate) should serve as the Phase 1 hard floor, and what composite weight against dispersion rank preserves daily rebalancing throughput while meeting the >~1.5% realized ROI benchmark?

Local indexed research (updates 122–124, 140–141) prescribes **bid-ask spread normalized by ATR** as the Phase 1 liquidity-depth hard floor for Cosmo/Wanda’s custom RemotePairlist, with **estimated slippage on entry** as an acceptable alternative proxy. This metric is chosen over raw order-book depth because it directly proxies exit actionability and spread cost relative to realized volatility, aligning with the finding that the Top 20 edge is driven by “far more actionable exit opportunities and better liquidity alignment.”

The recommended composite is explicitly **not a fractional blended score** but a **rank-and-floor architecture**: **dispersion rank (Jade-style cross-sectional standard deviation and divergence_z) carries 100% of the ordinal ranking weight**, while the liquidity proxy functions as a **binary eligibility gate (hard floor, pass/fail)** with zero contribution to the ranking score. This structure is mandated by the cautionary evidence from The Turners’ 0-trade shift (0.0/24h pace, C grade), which proved that over-gating universe construction chokes throughput. By making liquidity a floor rather than a narrow inclusion gate or a blended score component, the daily 20-pair rebalancing velocity of the incumbent MarketCapPairList (refresh_period: 86400, number_assets: 20) is preserved.

The indexed test plan sets the success benchmark at **>~1.5% per-trade realized ROI** (versus the incumbent Cosmo/Wanda Top 20 baseline of ~1.75%) and an **unrealized-to-realized ratio below ~1.0×** (versus baseline ~0.86–0.93×). The exact quantitative threshold for the spread/ATR floor is left as a live-calibration parameter (notated as “X%” in the research artifacts) to be tuned from telemetry without altering the rank-and-floor architecture.

title: Phase 1 Liquidity Hard Floor: Bid-Ask Spread / ATR with Rank-and-Floor Architecture
content:
Focus question: What specific liquidity-depth proxy metric (e.g., bid-ask spread normalized by ATR, order-book depth, or slippage estimate) should serve as the Phase 1 hard floor, and what composite weight against dispersion rank preserves daily rebalancing throughput while meeting the >~1.5% realized ROI benchmark?

Local indexed research (updates 122–124, 140–141, 144–145) prescribes bid-ask spread normalized by ATR as the Phase 1 liquidity-depth hard floor for Cosmo/Wanda’s custom RemotePairlist, with estimated slippage on entry as an acceptable alternative proxy. Focus question: What specific liquidity-depth proxy metric (e.g., bid-ask spread normalized by ATR, order-book depth, or slippage estimate) should serve as the Phase 1 hard floor, and what composite weight against dispersion rank preserves daily rebalancing throughput while meeting the >~1.5% realized ROI benchmark?

Local indexed research (updates 122–124, 140–141, 144–151) prescribes bid-ask spread normalized by ATR as the Phase 1 liquidity-depth hard floor for Cosmo/Wanda’s custom RemotePairlist, with estimated slippage on entry as an acceptable alternative proxy. Order-book depth is explicitly disfavored because spread/ATR directly proxies exit actionability and spread cost relative to realized volatility, aligning with the finding that the Top 20 edge is driven by “far more actionable exit opportunities and better liquidity alignment.” The recommended composite architecture is explicitly not a fractional blended score but a rank-and-floor design: dispersion rank (Jade-style cross-sectional standard deviation and divergence_z) carries 100% of the ordinal ranking weight, while the liquidity proxy functions as a binary eligibility gate (hard floor, pass/fail) with zero contribution to the ranking score. This structure is mandated by the cautionary evidence from The Turners’ 0-trade shift (0.0/24h pace, C grade), which proved that over-gating universe construction chokes throughput. By making liquidity a floor rather than a narrow inclusion gate or blended component, the daily 20-pair rebalancing velocity of the incumbent MarketCapPairList (refresh_period: 86400, number_assets: 20) is preserved. The indexed test plan sets success benchmarks at >~1.5% per-trade realized ROI (versus the incumbent Cosmo/Wanda Top 20 baseline of ~1.75%) and an unrealized-to-realized ratio below ~1.0× (versus baseline ~0.86–0.93×). The exact quantitative threshold for the spread/ATR floor is intentionally left as a live-calibration parameter (notated as “X%”) to be tuned from telemetry without altering the rank-and-floor architecture.

title: Phase 1 Liquidity Hard Floor & Rank-and-Floor Architecture for Cosmo/Wanda RemotePairlist
content:
Focus question: What specific liquidity-depth proxy metric (e.g., bid-ask spread normalized by ATR, order-book depth, or slippage estimate) should serve as the Phase 1 hard floor, and what composite weight against dispersion rank preserves daily rebalancing throughput while meeting the >~1.5% realized ROI benchmark?

Local indexed research (updates 122–124, 140–141, and 144–158) prescribes bid-ask spread normalized by ATR as the Phase 1 liquidity-depth hard floor for Cosmo/Wanda’s custom RemotePairlist, with estimated slippage on entry as an acceptable alternative proxy. Raw order-book depth is explicitly disfavored because spread/ATR directly proxies exit actionability and spread cost relative to realized volatility, aligning with the finding that the Top 20 edge is driven by far more actionable exit opportunities and better liquidity alignment.

The recommended composite architecture is explicitly not a fractional blended score but a rank-and-floor design: dispersion rank (Jade-style cross-sectional standard deviation and divergence_z) carries 100% of the ordinal ranking weight, while the liquidity proxy functions as a binary eligibility gate (hard floor, pass/fail) with zero contribution to the ranking score. This structure is mandated by the cautionary evidence from The Turners’ 0-trade shift (0.0/24h pace, C grade), which proved that over-gating universe construction chokes throughput. By making liquidity a floor rather than a narrow inclusion gate or blended component, the daily 20-pair rebalancing velocity of the incumbent MarketCapPairList (refresh_period: 86400, number_assets: 20) is preserved.

The indexed test plan sets success benchmarks at >~1.5% per-trade realized ROI (versus the incumbent Cosmo/Wanda Top 20 baseline of ~1.75%) and an unrealized-to-realized ratio below ~1.0× (versus baseline ~0.86–0.93×). The exact quantitative threshold for the spread/ATR floor is intentionally left as a live-calibration parameter (notated as “X%”) to be tuned from telemetry without altering the rank-and-floor architecture.

title: Telemetry-Derived Heuristic for Spread/ATR Hard Floor Live-Calibration (X%)
content:
Focus question: What telemetry-derived heuristic or historical distribution analysis should determine the initial live-calibration value 'X%' for the bid-ask spread / ATR hard floor, ensuring the daily 20-pair rebalancing throughput is preserved while the >~1.5% realized ROI benchmark remains attainable?

Local indexed research (updates 122–124, 140–141, 144–164) prescribes a rank-and-floor architecture for Cosmo/Wanda’s RemotePairlist in which dispersion rank carries 100% of the ordinal weight and bid-ask spread normalized by ATR serves as a binary eligibility gate (hard floor, pass/fail) with zero contribution to the ranking score. The exact threshold X% is intentionally left as a live-calibration parameter to be tuned from telemetry without altering this architecture.

To satisfy the dual constraints—preserving the daily 20-pair rebalancing throughput (incumbent MarketCapPairList baseline: ~17.9 projected closed trades per 24h) and keeping the >~1.5% per-trade realized ROI attainable (versus the Cosmo/Wanda Top 20 baseline of ~1.75%)—the initial X% should be determined by a rolling empirical percentile analysis of the spread/ATR distribution across the full candidate universe (e.g., Top 50) over the same lookback window used for dispersion scoring.

Throughput preservation heuristic: Set X% at approximately the 75th–80th percentile of the observed spread/ATR distribution. This guarantees that at least 25–30 pairs clear the binary floor, providing a buffer above the required 20-pair slate and directly preventing the cautionary throughput collapse seen in The Turners’ 0-trade shift (0.0/24h pace, C grade), where over-gating choked universe construction.

ROI attainment validation: Filter incumbent Cosmo/Wanda trade telemetry to include only entries where the pair’s pre-trade spread/ATR was ≤ the candidate X%. The realized ROI of this filtered subset must remain above the >~1.5% benchmark (with headroom toward the ~1.75% baseline). If the filtered ROI sags below 1.5%, tighten X% incrementally; if throughput stays healthy and ROI exceeds the benchmark comfortably, maintain or slightly loosen the floor to improve resilience.

Bootstrap shortcut in absence of full RemotePairlist history: Derive the initial X% from the historical spread/ATR distribution of the incumbent MarketCapPairList Top 20 at actual trade entry times. Use the 90th percentile of that distribution as the starting hard ceiling—this represents the worst liquidity condition that still historically supported the ~1.75% baseline ROI. Live calibration then iterates from this telemetry-derived anchor, adjusting X% solely in response to observed pass-through pair count and realized ROI drift, while keeping the rank-and-floor architecture fixed.

Local indexed research (updates 122–124, 140–141, 144–164, 168–172) prescribes a rank-and-floor architecture for Cosmo/Wanda’s RemotePairlist in which dispersion rank carries 100% of the ordinal weight and bid-ask spread normalized by ATR serves as a binary eligibility gate (hard floor, pass/fail) with zero contribution to the ranking score. The exact threshold X% is intentionally left as a live-calibration parameter tuned from telemetry without altering this architecture.

Primary Heuristic — Rolling Empirical Percentile Analysis
The initial X% should be derived from a rolling empirical percentile analysis of the spread/ATR distribution across the full candidate universe (e.g., Top 50) over the same lookback window used for dispersion scoring.

• Throughput Preservation Constraint: Set X% at approximately the 75th–80th percentile of the observed spread/ATR distribution. This guarantees that at least 25–30 pairs clear the binary floor, providing a buffer above the required 20-pair slate and directly preventing the cautionary throughput collapse observed in The Turners’ 0-trade shift (0.0/24h pace, C grade). The incumbent MarketCapPairList baseline projects ~17.7–17.9 closed trades per 24h (Cosmo/Wanda Top 20 telemetry: 66 closed trades over ~89.6 runtime hours, avg_roi ~1.79%); maintaining this pace requires sufficient pair pass-through.

• ROI Attainment Validation: Filter incumbent Cosmo/Wanda Top 20 trade telemetry to include only entries where the pair’s pre-trade spread/ATR was ≤ the candidate X%. The realized ROI of this filtered subset must remain above the >~1.5% benchmark, with headroom toward the ~1.75% baseline. If the filtered ROI sags below 1.5%, tighten X% incrementally; if throughput stays healthy and ROI exceeds the benchmark comfortably, maintain or slightly loosen the floor to improve resilience.

Bootstrap Shortcut in Absence of Full RemotePairlist History
Derive the initial X% from the historical spread/ATR distribution of the incumbent MarketCapPairList Top 20 at actual trade entry times. Use the 90th percentile of that distribution as the starting hard ceiling—this represents the worst liquidity condition that still historically supported the ~1.75% baseline ROI. Live calibration then iterates from this telemetry-derived anchor, adjusting X% solely in response to observed pass-through pair count and realized ROI drift, while keeping the rank-and-floor architecture fixed.
